# Control arms and bushings

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Inspect driver's rear cam bolt for seizure and use anti-seize or cut out seized bolts. [t373]

Select a lower control arm brand, noting that OEM parts are often preferred over aftermarket options for durability. [t550]

[Partial] Drop the control arm and heat mounting tabs to soften metal before installation. [t698]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Select a lower control arm brand, noting that OEM parts are often preferred over aftermarket options for durability.
2. Consider enhanced bushings if the original setup suffered from wear or clunking noises.

_Procedure reported by [t550]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t698] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Drop the control arm from the vehicle.
2. Heat the UCA or LCA mounting tabs to soften the metal.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t373] [Partial]</summary>

1. Inspect the driver's rear cam bolt for seizure.

</details>

## Tools

- [Partial] Hydraulic rams [t698]

## Parts

- [Partial] Anti-seize compound [t373]
- Lower Control Arm: OEM, Moog, AC Delco, Mevotech, Dorman, ADO Enhanced [t550]
- [Partial] New LCA bushings [t373]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Use a generous amount of anti-seize on the cam bolt. [t373]
- [Partial] If cutting out a seized OEM eccentric bolt, replace with new ones. [t373]
- Check if the ball joints are still in good condition before replacing just the bushings. [t550]
- [Partial] Look for arms with weld washers to ensure proper seating. [t550]
- Use heat instead of hydraulic pressure if cost is a concern. [t698]
- Accept that this method suits older, less critical trail rigs. [t698]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Choosing Dorman parts which may wear out quickly under heavy abuse. [t550]
- [Partial] Ignoring low-pressure zirconium fittings that might not clear CV joints on premium Mevotech units. [t550]
